content: Lenacapavir, a moderate inhibitor of the CYP3A4 enzyme, can increase the levels or effects of various medications that are metabolized by this enzyme. This interaction occurs because lenacapavir affects the hepatic and intestinal metabolism of these drugs, potentially leading to an increased risk of adverse reactions. The effects of lenacapavir on CYP3A4 substrates may persist for up to nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. For medications such as brexpiprazole, bromocriptine, buprenorphine (in various formulations including buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection), buspirone, busulfan, cabozantinib, calcifediol, cannabidiol, capivasertib, carbamazepine, cariprazine, ceritinib, chloroquine, chlorpheniramine, ciclesonide (inhaled and intranasal), cilostazol, cisapride, citalopram, clarithromycin, clonazepam, clorazepate, cobicistat, cobimetinib, cocaine (topical), colchicine, conivaptan, conjugated estrogens, copanlisib, cortisone, crizotinib, cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine, dabigatran, dabrafenib, daclatasvir, danicopan, dantrolene, dapsone, daridorexant, darifenacin, darolutamide, darunavir, dasatinib, deflazacort, dexamethasone, dexlansoprazole, diazepam (including buccal and intranasal formulations), digoxin, diltiazem, disopyramide, docetaxel, doravirine, doxorubicin (including liposomal formulations), dronabinol, dronedarone, duvelisib, edoxaban, elagolix, elbasvir/grazoprevir, eletriptan, eliglustat, elvitegravir, enfurtumab vedotin, and others, caution is advised. When co-administering lenacapavir with these drugs, it is essential to monitor for clinical signs and symptoms of toxicity or adverse effects. Dose adjustments may be necessary, and in some cases, starting with the lowest feasible dose of the co-administered drug is recommended. For example, when using deflazacort, the dose should be reduced to one-third of the recommended dosage. In cases where lenacapavir is initiated while the patient is already on a CYP3A4 substrate, or vice versa, careful titration and monitoring are required to achieve the desired therapeutic effect while minimizing the risk of toxicity.
